title: My Nature Journal
tagline: 36 journal prompts · Every season · Draw, notice, wonder
goal: 36 nature journal prompts for any season: map the sounds around you, adopt a tree, catch a snowflake on a mitten, watch buds open. Your kid draws what they see, then writes three short lines: what they notice, what they wonder, what it reminds them of. The cards are for you; the full journal at the end of the guide has a page for every card, ready to print, or use any notebook. Over a year, it becomes a real record of their place.
need: These cards, on your phone or printed
Any notebook, or print the journal pages at the end of the guide
A pencil, and something to sit on outside

lesson.text: A naturalist's journal isn't about pretty drawings. It's a record of looking closely. Under every drawing, three short lines turn a sketch into thinking.

model.line: A big maple leaf, with arrows to the stem and the holes.
Three holes near the edge, and the veins all start at the stem.
What made the holes? A caterpillar, or hail?
The veins look like the map of rivers near our house.

lesson.modelNote: Same leaf, but now it's real observation. When your kid says 'done,' ask: what do you notice, what do you wonder, what does it remind you of?

academics.subject: Science
academics.text: observing plants, animals, weather and seasonal change

academics.subject: Writing
academics.text: precise descriptions, questions, comparisons and short poems

academics.subject: Art
academics.text: scientific drawing: shapes, details, labels and arrows

academics.subject: Life skills
academics.text: slowing down, patience, and noticing change over time

howTo.intro: You don't need to know any plant or bird names. Read the card, sit with your kid, and journal too if you like: kids take it more seriously when you have your own page. Drawing comes first, words second, and nobody grades the art.

plan.what: Pick a card that fits the season, and grab a notebook and pencil.
10 to 20 minutes: draw first, then the three lines. Add the date and weather.
Share one wonder each. Flip back through old pages once a month.

troubleshoot.a: It's a record, not art. Shapes, labels and arrows count. Draw for 3 minutes, then write.

troubleshoot.q: They write one word and stop
troubleshoot.a: Use the three starters out loud: I notice, I wonder, it reminds me of. Let them answer by talking first.

skills.name: Curiosity
skills.text: turning what they see into questions

levelsLine: Three levels on every card. Explore: draw it and say one thing you notice. Develop: add the three lines. Extend: do the Deeper part and come back to the same spot in another season.

cards.name: Small Details
cards.t: Choose one small thing: a mushroom, a flower, a bug. Draw it bigger than real life.
cards.d: Describe its texture and smell in three words each.
cards.jp: Look closely at a small part of nature, like a flower or a mushroom. Draw it up close and describe its texture and smell.

cards.name: Sound Map
cards.t: Sit still for 3 minutes. Put yourself in the middle of the page and draw each sound where it comes from.
cards.d: Which sound was closest? Which one was farthest?
cards.jp: Sit quietly and listen to the sounds around you. Draw a map showing where each sound comes from.

cards.name: Cloud Stories
cards.t: Draw the shapes you see in the clouds right now.
cards.d: Write a short story about one of the clouds.
cards.jp: Look at the clouds and draw the shapes you see. Write a short story about one of the clouds.

cards.name: Adopt a Tree
cards.t: Pick a tree near home. Draw its shape, one leaf and a bark rubbing.
cards.d: Visit it once a season and draw it again on a new page.
cards.jp: Find a tree you like. Draw its leaves and bark, and write how you think it might change through the seasons.

cards.name: Animal Watch
cards.t: Watch one animal or insect for 2 minutes. Draw what it's doing.
cards.d: Where do you think it lives? What is it looking for?
cards.jp: Spot an animal or an insect. Draw what you see and describe what it does. Where do you think it lives?

cards.name: Weather Report
cards.t: Draw the sky. Write the temperature, the wind and how it feels outside.
cards.d: What will the weather do next? Check tomorrow.
cards.jp: Look at the weather today. Draw the sky and describe how you feel outside. What changes do you notice?

cards.name: Shape Hunt
cards.t: Find a circle, a spiral and a triangle in nature. Draw each one.
cards.d: Why might a plant or an animal be that shape?
cards.jp: Find different shapes in nature, like circles, triangles or spirals. Draw them and describe where you found them.

cards.name: Rock Portrait
cards.t: Find a rock that interests you. Draw it and describe its colour, texture and shape.
cards.d: Where do you think it came from, and how did it get here?
cards.jp: Find a rock that interests you. Draw it and describe its texture, colour and shape. Where do you think it comes from?

cards.name: Wind Watch
cards.t: Draw how the wind moves the grass, the leaves or the water.
cards.d: Write where you think the wind is going next.
cards.jp: Feel the wind on your face. Draw the wind moving through the trees or the grass, and write a story about where the wind is going.

cards.name: Insect-Eye View
cards.t: Get down low. Draw the world the way a beetle sees it.
cards.d: Write about the beetle's day, from its point of view.
cards.jp: Imagine you are an insect. Draw what the world looks like from down there, and write about your day.

cards.name: Colour Palette
cards.t: Find 6 different colours in nature. Make a swatch of each and name it.
cards.d: Give your palette a name, like 'Rainy Trail'.
cards.jp: Make a colour palette by finding different colours in nature. Draw and name the colours you find.

cards.name: Nature Poem
cards.t: Write a 3-line poem about something you see or hear right now.
cards.d: Draw a small picture beside your poem.
cards.jp: Write a short poem inspired by something you see or hear in nature today. Draw a picture to go with your poem.

cards.name: Falling Leaf
cards.t: Watch a leaf fall. Draw its path from the branch to the ground.
cards.d: What will happen to the leaf next? Write its journey.
cards.jp: Watch and draw a leaf falling. Write about its journey from the branch to the ground, and what might happen to it next.

cards.name: Getting Ready
cards.t: Choose an animal and draw how it gets ready for winter.
cards.d: How does it stay warm or find food when it's cold?
cards.jp: Choose an animal and draw how it gets ready for winter (thicker fur, a hiding place...). Write about what this animal does to stay warm.

cards.name: Leaf Investigation
cards.t: Pick up a leaf. Draw it and label the stem, the veins and the edge.
cards.d: How does each part help the plant?
cards.jp: Pick up a leaf. Draw it and label its parts. Write how each part helps the plant stay healthy.

cards.name: Wild Homes
cards.t: Find a place an animal might live: a hole, a nest, a hollow log. Draw it.
cards.d: Who might live there? What clues tell you?
cards.jp: Find a place where an animal might live, like a hole in a tree or a nest. Draw it and write about who might live there.

cards.name: Seed Hunt
cards.t: Find 3 different seeds. Draw each one beside how you think it travels.
cards.d: Which seed would travel the farthest? Why?

cards.name: Mushroom Watch
cards.t: Find a mushroom. Draw the top, the underside and where it grows. Look, don't touch.
cards.d: Come back in 3 days. What changed?

cards.name: Same Spot, New Season
cards.t: Draw one spot as it is today, then draw it the way you think it will look in winter.
cards.d: Come back in winter and check your prediction.
cards.jp: Describe how this place might look in another season. Draw it today, then draw it the way you imagine it will change.

cards.name: Leaf Mandala
cards.t: Make a circle design with fallen leaves on the ground. Draw it.
cards.d: Why did you put the colours in that order?
cards.jp: Collect small things from nature, like leaves, stones or twigs, and arrange them into a mandala. Draw it.

cards.name: Winter Sounds
cards.t: Stand still in the snow. Draw a sound map of winter: crunch, drip, wind.
cards.d: How are winter sounds different from summer sounds?
cards.jp: Sit quietly and listen to the sounds of winter, like snow crunching underfoot or wind in the trees. Draw a sound map and write how these sounds make you feel.

cards.name: Winter Sky
cards.t: Draw the winter sky and the light at this time of day.
cards.d: What time does it get dark now? Write it down each week.
cards.jp: Look at the sky in winter. Draw the winter clouds. Write about how the sky changes in winter.

cards.name: Snowflakes Up Close
cards.t: Catch snowflakes on a dark mitten. Draw three different shapes.
cards.d: How many points does each one have?
cards.jp: Look closely at snowflakes. Draw their shapes and write what you find fascinating about them.

cards.name: After the Storm
cards.t: Draw the landscape during a snowfall, then again after.
cards.d: What changed? What disappeared under the snow?
cards.jp: Draw the landscape during and after a snowstorm. Write about the changes you see.

cards.name: Under the Snow
cards.t: Draw what you think is happening under the snow: sleeping animals, waiting plants.
cards.d: Write a story about one of them.
cards.jp: Imagine what is happening under the snow, where animals hide and plants wait for spring. Draw this hidden world and write a story about it.

cards.name: Bare Branches
cards.t: Choose a tree with no leaves. Draw its branches and buds.
cards.d: What will this tree look like in spring?
cards.jp: Choose a tree and look at it without its leaves. Draw its branches and imagine how the tree feels in winter. Write about how it gets ready for spring.

cards.name: Tracks in the Snow
cards.t: Find tracks in the snow. Draw them and the path they make.
cards.d: Who made them? Where were they going?
cards.jp: Look for animal tracks. Draw the tracks and guess which animal made them. Write a story about where the animal was going.

cards.name: Ice Patterns
cards.t: Find frost or ice. Draw the patterns you see up close.
cards.d: What shapes repeat? Where else have you seen them?

cards.name: First Shoots
cards.t: Find something new poking out of the ground. Draw it.
cards.d: Draw it again in one week. How much did it grow?
cards.jp: Look for the first shoots coming out of the soil. Draw them and write about what these young plants will become.

cards.name: Spring Rain
cards.t: Watch the rain. Draw the drops, the puddles and the ripples.
cards.d: How does rain help nature wake up?
cards.jp: Watch a rainy spring day. Draw the raindrops or the puddles and write about how rain helps nature wake up.

cards.name: Soil Detective
cards.t: Dig up a small scoop of soil. Draw the roots, bugs and stones you find.
cards.d: Put it all back. What lives in soil, and why?
cards.jp: Dig up a little soil and look at what you find. Draw and describe the roots, insects or stones you see.

cards.name: Bud Watch
cards.t: Find a branch with buds. Draw one bud every few days as it opens.
cards.d: Does it turn into a leaf or a flower?
cards.jp: Look at the buds on the trees. Draw a bud and write about how it turns into a leaf or a flower.

cards.name: New Nests
cards.t: Look for a nest in a tree or a bush. Draw it from a distance.
cards.d: What do you think it's made of? Who built it?
cards.jp: Look for bird nests in trees or bushes. Draw a nest and write about the birds that might live there and raise their young.

cards.name: Flower Focus
cards.t: Find one flower. Draw its petals, stem and leaves in detail.
cards.d: Count the petals. Do other flowers of the same kind match?
cards.jp: Find a flower. Draw it in detail, with its petals, stem and leaves. Write about how it might change as it grows.

cards.name: First Insects
cards.t: Find the first insects of spring. Draw them and what they're doing.
cards.d: Why do you think they're out now and not in winter?

cards.name: Puddle and Pond Life
cards.t: Look closely at the edge of a puddle or pond. Draw what moves.
cards.d: Come back in a week. What changed?

conclusion.headline: Your kid just started a real naturalist's journal.
conclusion.text: They looked closely, drew what they saw, and turned it into notices, wonders and comparisons. Observation, scientific drawing and writing, in a notebook that grows with every season.
conclusion.celebrate: Flip back through the pages together and point to a wonder: 'You asked what made those holes. Did you ever find out?'
extensions: Pick one spot and journal it every season for a year
Start a family journal: everyone adds a page on the same walk
Look up the answer to one 'I wonder' each week
Take the journal on your next trip and compare places

signs: They stop on walks to look closely at something
They ask 'I wonder...' questions on their own
They notice when something has changed since last time
makeItReal: Bring the journal everywhere for a month: the backyard, a park, a road trip stop. At the end of the month, read it together. Kids are amazed by how much they noticed, and it's a record you'll keep for years.

photo.alt: A boy in a yellow jacket and knit hat sitting on a camp chair in the snow, sketching the lake as snow falls
photo.caption: A sit spot on a snowy day: sketching the lake while the snow falls.

fromHome.text: On a snowy day, my son set up a camp chair on the shore and sketched the lake while the snow fell. It was his idea: a sit spot moment, one place, one chair, and time to really look. Nobody told him what to draw.
